newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower after Wall Street fall.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower after Wall Street fall.

text.p: French stocks opened sharply lower on Monday after a 2.27 percent fall in the Dow Jones industrial average on Friday.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index, which lost 1.28 percent on Friday, opened 1.36 percent lower at 2,539.43 points.
It fell to a low of 2,528.30 points, then bounced off a support level at 2,527-33 points to return to around 2,540 in the first hour of trade.
The CAC-40 April futures was 26 points lower at 2,540.
"The market's looking pretty resilient. Wall Street was down, but the dollar is looking very solid," a trader said.
Brokers said the CAC index has major support at 2,500.
Volume was 900 million francs in the first 40 minutes.

Shares in SGS-Thomson fell even more sharply than the market, falling 4.9 percent to 373.50 francs after the chip maker reported a drop in first-quarter net income to $90.50 million from $175 million.

Cie de Suez shares rose 1.35 percent to 285.10 francs after resuming trade on Monday. Traders said the market was pleased with the planned merger with Lyonnaise des Eaux announced on Friday and Suez's decision to triple the dividend.
Lyonnaise shares were down 0.93 percent at 535 francs.
Canal Plus's stock extended a recent rise fuelled by its increased weighting in the CAC index. Its Canalsatellite business said it expected its digital channel collection to break even in 1998.
